title: Good Firms vs. Good Deals – They’re Not the Same (and Why That Matters)

 Good Firms vs. Good Deals – They’re Not the Same (and Why That Matters)
Hi Sara,
If you’re on the hunt for an accounting firm to buy, you’ve probably caught yourself scrolling listings like it’s late-night Zillow—dreaming of that perfect cloud-based beauty with remote staff and sky-high margins. 
But here’s a little reality check: the “perfect” firm doesn’t always mean the “perfect” deal. And if you mix those up? You could end up with a cash flow nightmare instead of your next big win. 
Let’s break down why terms matter just as much as the firm—and how knowing the difference could save you from overpaying your way into buyer’s remorse.
I spent most of my week talking to buyers—and when Letter of Intent season is in full swing, you know it feels a lot like musical chairs:
Tax season slows things down.

May and June? Buyers flood in, offers fly.

July and August? Closings heat up.

September 15 & October 15 deadlines creep up—panic.

Then it’s holidays, and boom, back to tax season.

When this happens, buyers are scanning listings, making snap judgments:
✅ Cloud-based firm, great margins? Good deal.
❌ Local, paper-based, not remote? Bad deal.
Except… that’s not how this works.
A good firm doesn’t always equal a good deal.
Why? Because a good deal is the firm + the terms.
You need both to make the math work:
Good firm, bad terms? Overpay, and it won’t cash flow. You’re toast.

Less desirable firm, great terms? Might be your best deal yet.

I hear this all the time: “But this firm is perfect—remote team, owner works on the business, not in it.”
(Yes, we should all drink every time someone says that.)
But if you’re paying 10x earnings? That’s not a dream. That’s a future bankruptcy filing.
On the flip side, a “meh” firm—local clients, paper-based—might be a home run if you negotiate seller financing, a lower price, or better transition support.
My grandmother used to say: There’s a lid for every pot.
And in this market, there’s a deal structure that can make almost any firm a win—if you know how to write your LOI and set the right terms.
So, if you’re hunting for the perfect firm… maybe what you really need is the perfect deal structure.
If you want help making that happen, check out Deal Academy, where I break this all down.
Cheers (and to smart deals),
Sarah Sharp
Partner, SK&S Law Group
Founder, Deal Academy
